gcp._note: This is GCP's NetworkPeering, embedded on Network.peerings rather than returned by a standalone listing API (see gcp_network_mcp.models.peering.NetworkPeering) -- native_id is therefore a synthesized 'projects/.../networks/.../peerings/<name>' identifier, not a native self_link (GCP peerings have none of their own). remote_network_urn is null and remote_native_id is populated instead: partner-vpc lives in project acme-partner-services-654321, a scope this collection's credentials cannot read into (no cross-project IAM binding visible), so the peer network cannot be resolved to a RESOURCE node -- see the paired UNRESOLVED node in topology-graph.gcp-vpc-topology.json and its CollectionWarning. allow_forwarded_traffic is null: GCP's NetworkPeering has no matching field at all (that concept is Azure-specific); exchange_subnet_routes/import_custom_routes/export_custom_routes are GCP's own genuine, directly-observed fields, unlike for an AWS-sourced Peering where this contract's docstring says those must stay null.
